items.title: Meet Martini: A Film Set for AI Video That Aims to Help Filmmakers Streamline Their Shots
items.excerpt: Martini is a collaborative, web-based platform pitched as a virtual 'film set' for AI video production: filmmakers get real cinematic controls — fly around a 2D/3D scene and operate a virtual camera to find coverage — instead of prompt-roulette with generative video models. It doubles as a real-time collaborative pre-production hub with NLE-compatible timeline and XML export, launching freemium with paid tiers from $15/month.

items.title: Puget Systems at SIGGRAPH 2026: The Robo Dojo
items.excerpt: RedShark's SIGGRAPH 2026 report on the Puget Systems Robo Dojo booth highlights Beeble AI and District Cinema demonstrating the AI lighting workflow behind Corridor Crew's 'Son of a Dungeon' Season 3: SwitchLight 3 generates physically based rendering passes for relighting and scene reconstruction from 4K cinematic footage, then feeds them into Unreal Engine for real-time rendering on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell workstation.

items.title: The rise of the independent AI-assisted developer tools: warnings and considerations
items.excerpt: ProVideo Coalition's Jeff Greenberg examines the flood of small, AI-assisted independent tools now entering post-production pipelines, sorting them into 'Gold Rush' profit plays vs genuine 'Problem Solver' utilities. He lays out five questions editors and facilities should ask before trusting one on client work — maintenance if the developer vanishes, API/platform compatibility, documented failure conditions, credential/data security, and update cadence — arguing that in a craft where reliability is the product, unvetted AI tools are accumulated risk.
